speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you're an infant with recurrent stridor and wheezing; to help you, could you tell me at what age these episodes started and if they happen specifically during feeding, crying, or lying down?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia.

The combination of stridor worsening with neck flexion (chin-to-chest position) during crying and feeding, along with recurrent vomiting, is classic for this condition. No further tests are needed at this time.
